correctness.rationale: PASS: The exact source codebooks have the claimed lengths, cardinalities, and minimum distances 9,9,11; the independent bitwise count found pair-near edges 2064/7288/1517, near triangles 20388/79312/16965, valid fourfold centers 8/96/0 with all valid quartet centers distinct. For d>=2r-1, any r-ball-common pair has distance 2r-1 or 2r and has exactly binomial(2r,r) common centers, even in the odd-distance case. Every triple common center equals its binary coordinate-majority, which is forced by error-support disjointness; thus each near triangle contributes one center. A valid quadruple has a unique common center; if a five-list existed it would force at least five four-tuples sharing one center, contradicting distinctness. Inverting moments m*Vol(n,r), E*binomial(2r,r), T, Q yields all five bins and totals 2^n. This is an exhaustive finite proof for these three explicit books, not a statement about every code of the same parameters or a general optimal-code theorem.

The complete size histogram determines the probability of any ambiguity, worst list size and counts of three- and four-way collisions for genuinely new high-density codes; the majority-center structural reduction is itself motivated and reusable. This is a self-contained, nontrivial exact finite invariant, not a restatement of the original packing bounds or an arbitrary parameter slice.
